question: There's a fire in my dorm, what do I do?

laptop.answer:
If you can, get out and away from the fire, smoke or gas right now, and don't go back in for anything. Then call 911 from a safe place. If you can't get out, call 911 right now and tell them where you are. RockyGPT can't send help or stay with you, so please call as soon as you can.

On campus, these published numbers can also help:

**Public Safety \(Emergency\)**: \(201\) 684-6666; \(201\) 684-7789; \(201\) 684-7011. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/)

question: How do I get a parking permit?

laptop.answer:
Apply online through the Parking Permits registration portal: https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/ [4, 11]. Section 7 instructs you to log on to the RCNJ Parking Permits site, enter permit type, complete contact information and vehicle information, review the request, then print or save the registration page with your request number; that page is verification, not the permit. Select the correct housing assignment or commuter status and “student,” not “faculty/staff.” [7]

The pages differ on application instructions: section 8 instead directs students to ThePermitStore.com, https://ramapo.thepermitstore.com/, and gives its steps: enter Ramapo as your destination; select Ramapo College of New Jersey; click Apply; agree to the terms; log in; complete personal information; select a permit; enter vehicle information; continue through payment (which should say “No Payment Necessary”); finish. It says you’ll receive account and order-approval emails, then print a temporary permit from “MY” and activate the mailed permanent permit on the site. [8]

The parking fee appears automatically on your term bill; it is not paid when applying. [4] New-student permits are picked up at New Student Check-In. Returning resident students pick theirs up from their on-campus mailbox. Returning commuter students pick up at the Public Safety ID Office Monday through Friday during normal operating hours, or at the Public Safety Office Main Desk after 3 pm if they email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu to request a different time. [2, 4, 7]

For help, contact Public Safety at parkingpermits@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7432; include your Ramapo student ID number (R#) when emailing. [3, 7]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq/)

question: Can I have an overnight guest in my residence hall?

laptop.answer:
Yes. Guests may stay in the halls if they follow Residence Life policies and do not disrupt building operations. Each registered guest may stay no more than 3 nights (consecutive or not) in any 7-day period; a night begins and ends at 10:00 PM. Residents may host up to 2 guests at a time. Guests must have valid ID, remain with their resident host at all times, and have access to their approved Guest Registration email if on campus after 10:00 PM. Current RCNJ residential students do not need guest registration. [1, 2]

For overnight stays, guests must be registered through the residence hall office/kiosk. [9] In shared housing, the College assumes roommates agree to guest registration; you can opt out by contacting your RA to arrange a roommate/suitemate/apartment contract. [1, 2] Residents are responsible for their guests. Guest misconduct can result in removal or a campus restriction ban. [1–3, 5]

Section 6 is a past Spring 2026 check-out notice: it says the last night for overnight guests was Monday, May 11, 2026. That date has passed and is not an upcoming deadline. [6]

Housing & Residence Life: reslife@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7461. Guest procedures: https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/ [1, 2]

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/spring-check-out/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

question: How do I drop a class?

laptop.answer:
The Registrar handles drop forms. Contact: reg@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7695, D-224. [3]

1. During the add/drop/100% refund period, drop online through Web Self Service. Courses dropped by the last day of add/drop will not appear on your transcript. Check the Academic Calendar for deadlines: https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/ [1][3]
2. During the 50% refund period, section 1 says to access a drop form online or at the Registrar’s Office and submit it there by the calendar deadline. Section 3 says you may drop in Web Self Service or submit a 50% Drop Form to the Registrar. The pages differ on the stated options. [1][3]
3. Section 4 also says to check the Academic Calendar for 100% drop deadlines and says students can drop on the Web through the end of add/drop. [4]

Check the Academic Calendar for the deadline for your term. [1][3][4][7] Dropping may affect financial aid, progress toward graduation, athletics, housing, or campus involvement; seek advisement as appropriate. [1] Deregistration is not an approved way to formally drop classes. [8]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/online-course-information/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/faq/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/payment-policies/)

question: How do I request a transcript?

laptop.answer:
The Registrar handles transcript requests. [1–5]

- Electronic: Request through the National Student Clearinghouse: https://tsorder.studentclearinghouse.org/school/select [5] (also listed here: https://nschelpcenter.force.com/student/s/). [1,6] Electronic transcripts have a fee; section 2 lists $4.90 per transcript request, while section 6 says to contact the Clearinghouse for pricing. [2,6] The download link is available for 30 days. [2]
- Paper: Complete the Official Transcript Request Form: https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Official-Transcript-Request-Form-FILLABLE.pdf [2,5] You may obtain it from the Registrar’s Office, by mail, fax or online; send the completed form by email, mail or fax to the Registrar’s Office. [2] Fax: (201) 684-7956. [2] Paper transcripts have no fee according to section 2; section 9 says a one-time flat fee entitles a student to unlimited official transcripts per career at no additional cost. The pages differ on charges. [2,9]
- Clear any holds before requesting. [2] If you attended before Fall 1988, you cannot order electronically; request by mail using the form. [2] If you don’t have an “R” number, use the last 4 digits of your Social Security Number. [2]

Paper processing is typically 3-5 business days (longer during peak periods). [2] Electronic processing is listed as typically 1-3 business days in section 2 and 24-48 business hours in section 8; the pages differ. [2,8] Contact the Registrar at reg@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7695, D-224. [1,2]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/forms-transcripts/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/)

question: How do I appeal a grade?

laptop.answer:
Grade appeals require supporting documentation. Possible grounds include a computational error, factual information unavailable when the grade was posted (such as submitted, ungraded work), or an alleged College Policy violation. Appeals based on wanting a higher GPA/transfer grade, or an academic-integrity penalty, are not considered. After a degree is conferred, its record is closed and cannot be adjusted. [1]

Undergraduates: Within 20 calendar days after grades are posted, email or send a certified letter to the course instructor with documentation. Both sides should try in good faith to resolve the disagreement; they have up to 15 calendar days. If they agree to an adjustment, the instructor sends an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request and supporting materials to the sponsoring unit’s Dean for approval, then to the Registrar. If you do not agree, submit a written appeal by email or certified letter, with relevant course materials/work, to that Dean within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. The Dean reviews the materials and has 15 calendar days to decide. [2]

The pages differ on whether the Dean’s decision is final: section 2 says a student may petition the Provost within 20 calendar days of the Dean’s final written decision, by written email or certified letter, with evidence the Dean made a factual mistake, violated policy, or acted outside the Dean’s purview; section 17 says the Dean’s decision is final. [2][17]

Graduate students: Within 20 calendar days of grade posting, write to the faculty member by email or certified letter and provide documentation. They have up to 15 calendar days to determine the grade. If they agree to an adjustment, the faculty member submits an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request and supporting materials to the sponsoring unit’s Dean for approval, then to the Registrar. If no agreement, send a written appeal with relevant course materials/work to the graduate program Director within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. The Director reviews it and recommends to the Dean for final approval. If the Director’s opinion is adverse, petition the supervising Dean in writing with your position and evidence contradicting the decision or information previously unavailable. [3]

For the undergraduate Provost petition, contact the Office of the Provost: provost@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7330, first floor of the Birch Mansion. [2]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature) [17](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#student-appeals-of-an-academic-nature)

question: How do I get a replacement ID card?

laptop.answer:
Public Safety handles ID card replacements. For a lost card, contact the ID Room at publicsafety@ramapo.edu; it will reprint the card and leave it at the front of the Public Safety Office for pickup, and email you when it is ready. The lost-card replacement fee is $25. If your card is damaged or not working, contact the ID Room; replacement is at no charge. [2]

For lost or stolen cards, deactivate it immediately by calling (201) 684-7789. A located card cannot be reactivated. To get a new card, visit the ID Card Room at C-101 or email publicsafety@ramapo.edu. [4] The ID Room is C-Wing, C-101; call (201) 684-6229. [3]

The pages differ on the replacement process: the student-card page says you “must go to the Public Safety ID Room (C-101)” for a lost or broken card and says a replacement fee applies [6], while the ID-card page gives email and pickup instructions, says a lost-card fee is $25, and says damaged/not-working cards are replaced at no charge [2]. The ID-card page also says to email the ID Room and make an appointment to get a new ID; its hours are Monday-Friday, 8:30am until 4:00pm. [1]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/id-cards/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/id-cards/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/id-cards/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/lost-found/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/)

question: Can freshmen bring a car to campus?

laptop.answer:
Yes. All students who plan to bring a vehicle to campus must read and follow the RCNJ Motor Vehicle Rules and Regulations [2]. Resident students planning to have a vehicle on campus must apply for and display a valid parking permit; register using the [parking permit registration link](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/opr/OPRMain.aspx?IsAuth=1&groupid=102&groupname=PUBLIC+SAFETY). The permit will be placed in your campus mailbox within seven days of approval [1]. Residents who need gate access must visit the Public Safety Parking and ID Office (C-101) to have their Ramapo ID coded; IDs are not automatically activated for gate access [3]. First-year students in Pine Hall may park only in D Lot [3]. Parking permits are issued based on College status, are non-transferable, and valid only for the vehicle assigned; resident students are limited to one permit [7].
For parking questions, email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu [1]. Public Safety (Non-Emergency): (201) 684-7432 [7].

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/new-student-guide/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/)

question: How do I report a lost item?

laptop.answer:
Public Safety handles lost property. Its page says the Department of Public Safety maintains a Lost and Found log at the Public Safety Office in C-Wing, C-102. To claim lost property, present your Ramapo College ID at the front desk; non-affiliates may present any government issued picture ID. [2] The employee handbook says, “If you lose an article, its loss should be reported there.” If it has been found, it will be kept awaiting your identification. [8]

Public Safety (Non-Emergency): (201) 684-7432; publicsafety@ramapo.edu; C-102. [2]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/lost-found/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/poerd/employee-handbook/)

question: How do I get a tutor?

laptop.answer:
Start with the option that matches your course:

- For math or science tutoring, the Math and Science Tutoring Center covers MATH 021–237, Fundamentals of Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Fundamentals of Biology, and Genetics. Go to G Wing, Room 131; it is free and no appointment is needed. The tutor/course schedule is posted by the G Wing, Room 131 entrance. Supervisor: Prof. Sara Kuplinsky, skuplins@ramapo.edu, G131A. [2]
- For STEM Center tutoring, use Connect to schedule an appointment or view walk-in hours; follow the [appointment instructions](https://www.ramapo.edu/connect/wp-content/uploads/sites/248/2023/10/Instructions-fot-student-STEM-Center-Appointments-Fa23.pdf). [5, 7] STEM Center: (201) 684-7345 (Tutoring Coordinator) or (201) 684-7774 (Director); G-131. [7]
- For writing, reading, or study skills, make an appointment with the Center for Reading and Writing through Connect. It offers one-on-one, face-to-face consultations. Hours: Mon.–Thurs. 10:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; Fri. 10:00 a.m.–2:00 p.m. Location: Linden Hall, 2nd floor, Room 211. Email crw@ramapo.edu or call (201) 684-7557. [4]
- You can also search tutoring resources at https://tutoring.ramapo.edu/. [3]

For help with a particular course, your instructor is also a good source; you can speak before or after class, visit during office hours, or email them. [9]

For Math for the Modern World, listed walk-ins require no appointment: Mon. 12:00–1:00 p.m. and 7:00–8:00 p.m.; Wed. 10:00–11:00 a.m.; Thurs. 11:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m. and 7:00–8:00 p.m.; Sat. 10:30–11:30 a.m. [8]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-resources/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-resources/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/campus-resources/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/stem-center/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/stem-center/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/families/faq/)
